dedupe_keys.name: canal automation at the central arizona irrigation and drainage district with sacman uscid 2010

description: This case study describes how the Central Arizona Irrigation and Drainage District automated its canals. The district began delivering water in 1989 and, though designed for automatic control, ran manually until staff built a home-made SCADA system; radio problems led it to modernise from 2002 with spread-spectrum radios, remote terminal units and a commercial SCADA package, and from 2005 to automate most check gates. At the time of writing 125 gates were under remote supervisory control, 129 water levels were monitored, and five lateral canals ran under full automatic control with SacMan, software from the U.S. Arid Land Agricultural Research Center that routes flow changes and corrects errors with downstream water level feedback, while automation of the main canal had been tested in simulation. It was written by Robert Strand and Albert Clemmens and presented at a U.S. Committee on Irrigation and Drainage conference in Sacramento in March 2010. It concerns one district in Arizona. The paper is available free online as a PDF in Colorado State University's Mountain Scholar repository. Caveats: automation was limited to gates with position sensors, and results are descriptive. For simulation it is a worked example of automatic control of an irrigation canal network, useful when modelling canal operations and their response to supply shortfalls. It is related to the Central California Irrigation District canal modernisation case study record in this catalogue.
